overview: I3203 is a degraded-instrument recovery event. The standard is to accept radar turn commands without a reliable heading system, transition to the BFI when primary displays are unreliable, and keep aircraft control ahead of checklist or radio workload.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: A no-gyro approach is available under radar control when the directional gyro or stabilized compass information is inoperative or unreliable.

children.text: Tell ATC the heading system is unreliable and request a no-gyro PAR, ASR, PAR without glideslope, or no-gyro vectors to a visual approach if conditions support it.
Comply with normal PAR or ASR configuration, minimums, lost-communication, and missed-approach procedures; no-gyro only changes how turns are commanded.
ATC may also initiate no-gyro vectors if they observe incorrect directional responses.
Before final, make all turns at standard rate unless the controller directs otherwise, and start the turn immediately when told "turn left" or "turn right."
Stop the turn immediately when told "stop turn."
On final, use half-standard-rate turns unless the controller directs another rate.
Acknowledge instructions unless ATC states no further acknowledgements are required.

The common errors are slow turn compliance, using the wrong turn rate, arriving on final late to before-approach configuration, and confusing missed-approach, climbout, and lost-communication instructions.

items.text: A BFI approach is the control plan when the PFD or primary attitude/air-data picture is unusable because of ADC, IRU, IAC, or display failures.

children.text: Transition to the BFI first, then stabilize straight-and-level flight before troubleshooting expands.
Use coordinated rudder and aileron to level the wings, set a known pitch attitude, and crosscheck airspeed, altitude, vertical speed, and performance.
Complete the applicable NATOPS emergency procedure only after the aircraft is under control.
The BFI does not present turn information like the PFD; use attitude, heading trend, and the 10 percent or 20 percent bank-start rules for half-standard-rate or standard-rate turns.
The sideslip indicator is on top of the roll pointer and moves with it, which looks different from the PFD.
The altimeter uses 20-foot increments, the heading display shows only a partial scale, and VSI is a digital readout with up or down trend.
Use small corrections. The BFI workload trap is overcontrolling because the display looks unfamiliar.
A BFI recovery may pair naturally with no-gyro vectors or a radar approach because ATC can reduce heading-reference workload while the pilot preserves attitude and performance.
If communications, transponder, or remaining avionics are degraded too, declare the emergency and ask for the simplest recovery that preserves terrain clearance and workload margin.

studyNotes.summary: Let radar control reduce the heading workload, transition to the BFI before troubleshooting, and fly the degraded-instrument approach with small corrections and clear missed-approach logic.

summary: No-gyro radar approach execution and BFI approach control after primary instrument failures.
title: No-Gyro Approach
